/* ---- top bar ---- */
/* ---- hero ---- */
/* The intro art is shown whole on phones, the way the site shows it, instead of
   being cropped to a fixed band, and its foot fades out to white. */
/* The band is exactly as tall as the artwork is at full width (1600 x 2576 =>
   161.0vw), so the key visual shows whole: nothing off the sides, nothing off
   the ends. Everything that rides on the picture is placed as a fraction of it
   (see the three notes below), which is what keeps the badges at the knees on
   every phone instead of only on the one the geometry was traced from. */
.uma-hero {
  position: relative; overflow: hidden; line-height: 0;
  height: 161vw; background: #379A2A;
}
/* 161vw against a 0.621 picture means cover has nothing left to trim */
.uma-hero-art {
  position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%;
  object-fit: cover; object-position: 50% 50%;
}
/* the key visual carries the badge stack itself, the way the official first
   screen does, so the badges sit on the artwork instead of in a band below it */
/* the band's foot dissolves into the page below it */
.uma-hero-wash {
  position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 20%;
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(239,254,231,0) 0%, rgba(239,254,231,.26) 44%,
              rgba(239,254,231,.58) 70%, rgba(239,254,231,.88) 88%, #EFFEE7 100%);
}
.uma-hero-stack {
  /* pinned to the foot of the picture rather than to a height: the badges keep
     the same distance from the bottom edge on every width, which is what stops
     them spilling out of the band on a 280 css fold */
  position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: auto; bottom: 12.5vw; z-index: 3;
  padding: 0 10.2%; line-height: normal;
}
.uma-hero-stack .uma-fan-caption {
  display: block; text-align: right; margin-bottom: 5px;
  font-family: "Roboto Condensed", roboto, Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: 11px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: .2px; color: #fff;
  text-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.5);
}
.uma-hero-stack .uma-fan-rows { margin-top: 0; }
/* .top-kv__left .-umamusume: width 6.1333vw, padding 3.2vw 1.6vw at 2.4vw/49.3333vw */
/* .top-kv__left .-umamusume: 6.1333vw wide, 21.7 css of that on screen, and the
   reference string fills 168.9 css of length. In a vertical writing mode the
   *block* axis is horizontal, so the horizontal padding is the first value — it
   was the second, which left a negative content box and pushed the letters
   through both walls of the pill. Type is sized so the string lands on 149 css,
   the strings the official page runs are all caps, spaced wide, and the full
   phone capture (Screenshot_20261118-180923.jpg, DPR 3.5) puts the capsule at
   21.7 x 164.3 with glyphs only 7.7 css tall: Roboto Condensed 600 at 2.9vw
   (cap 7.5) with .5vw of tracking lands the ink on 158 and the capsule on 166. */
.uma-side {
  position: absolute; right: 2.4vw; top: 34.44vw; width: 6.3vw; color: #fff;
  /* Roboto, not Roboto Condensed: the site's plaque is a regular-width face —
     its capitals are as wide as they are tall (7.4 css each at a 7.43 pitch),
     which is why it fills 164 css with no tracking at all. */
  font-family: roboto, "Roboto Condensed", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: 3.07vw; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0; line-height: 1;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  writing-mode: vertical-rl; white-space: nowrap;
  text-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.45);
  border: .2667vw solid rgba(255,255,255,.85); border-radius: 999px;
  /* the type stays at its measured size; the length the reference has comes
     from the space at the ends of the capsule. In vertical writing mode the
     first padding value runs along the text, so that is the one that grows. */
  padding: 3.98vw 1vw; text-align: center;
}
/* the call to action sits in the first badge row, left of the plates, the way
   Play Now sits beside the store badges on the official screen */
/* The call to action is the supplied wordmark, not drawn type: the supplied
   PNG carries the cream fill, the orange drop and the white keyline exactly, so
   the pill no longer has to imitate it with gradients and four drop-shadows.
   Its art is 5.12 : 1, so a 4.2vw height gives a 21.5vw mark — the width the
   drawn type needed at 21px — and it keeps that ratio at every phone width. */
.uma-playnow { display: flex; align-items: center; }
.uma-playnow img { display: block; width: auto; height: 4.2vw; }

/* the scroll cue: stacked letters down the right edge, the way the site runs it */
/* .top-kv__left .-scroll: right 3.7333vw, top 140.8vw */
.uma-scroll {

}

/* ---------- In the Works (the site's News band) ----------
   The official band is a pink frame with a leaning ribbon straddling its top
   left corner, white cards inside it and a pink pill under them. All of it is
   CSS: the frame is a border on a rounded box, the ribbon is a skew, the card
   tags are clipped flags. Geometry from the reference capture (070505, 360 css
   wide): the frame runs x 15.8 -> 345.1 with a 3.1 css #FF79D0 edge round a
   #FFF0F7 panel; the cards run x 34.7 -> 326.2 (291.5 wide) with 9.4 css
   between them; the ribbon runs x 10 -> 137, y 134.6 -> 169, 13 degrees off
   square. The ground is the pale horseshoe art, and the key visual's photograph
   fades straight into it above the frame. */
.uma-news {
  background: #EFFEE7; border-top: 0; overflow: visible;
  padding: 9.5vw 4.4vw 9vw;
  /* the band climbs into the key visual's fade, so the pale ground and the ribbon sit at the
     level where the picture was already dissolving, not 45 css below it */
  margin-top: -6vw;
}
/* The ground is a plain <img>, the way every other band in this profile carries its
   artwork. A CSS background-image here never reached the live page: the band came out as
   flat #EFFEE7 with the pattern missing, while the card art from the same commit loaded,
   so the url() is the only thing that could have failed. The image is 1000 x 1833, so at
   any width it is 1.833 x the width tall; where a band grows past that, the #EFFEE7 under
   it finishes the job. */
.uma-news-ground {
  position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 100%;
  height: 100%; object-fit: cover; object-position: center top;
  z-index: 0; pointer-events: none;
}
/* The artwork's first band is near-white and its top edge lands inside the picture now that
   the band climbs 6vw, so this overlay carries the band colour over that edge: transparent
   where the photograph still is, solid across the join, then handing over to the art. */
/* The last of the join. The key visual's own wash does the long part above; this covers the
   short stretch the band climbed into and hides the artwork's top edge, solid #EFFEE7 right
   across the band's first pixel, then handing over to the art below. */
.uma-news::after {
  content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: -8vw; height: 28vw; z-index: 0;
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(239,254,231,0) 0%, rgba(239,254,231,.45) 16%,
              #EFFEE7 29%, #EFFEE7 44%, rgba(239,254,231,.55) 74%,
              rgba(239,254,231,0) 100%);

}

/* Our copy of the About art is the landscape crop, 1100 x 688, while the official phone page
   runs a taller crop of the same painting, so the stands sit lower there. Covering a 360 x 446
   band with this one means showing about half of its width: the left half keeps the roofline
   low and the sky open, which is the reference's read, where centring it raised the stands
   across the whole right side. */
.uma-about .uma-sec-bg { object-position: 20% 50%; opacity: 1; }
/* The pink corner. On the reference the About art runs out under a pink diagonal with white
   showing past its lower edge, and that band is part of their taller crop: our window only
   reaches the middle of the wide painting, so the corner is drawn here instead, to the same
   geometry. Off the capture, at 3.5 px per css: the edge falls 0.42 css per css across the
   width, the band is 62 css deep, and its upper edge meets the right edge 112 css above the
   section's bottom. In vw that is 42.2, 17.2 and 31.1, on a 60vw tall plate at the bottom. */
.uma-about::before,
.uma-about::after {
  content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0;
  height: 60vw; z-index: 1; pointer-events: none;
}

  background: #FF6DC8;
  clip-path: polygon(0 80.6vw, 100% 38.3vw, 100% 53.9vw, 0 96.1vw);
}
.uma-about::after {
  background: #fff;
  clip-path: polygon(0 96.1vw, 100% 53.9vw, 100% 60vw, 0 60vw);
}

/* ---------- the site's own header bar (markup, not CSS art) ---------- */
/* No second header. The wordmark is pinned over Janitor's own profile bar and
   Janitor's title is made transparent behind it, so the site mark sits inside
   the real header instead of a copy of it. */
/* The wordmark rides inside Janitor's own bar. This row takes no height of its
   own: it is lifted straight onto their 44px bar and never paints a band, so
   there is no second header to see. Their bar keeps its blue from the page
   background (its own paint is cleared below), which also means the wordmark
   shows through even when their bar wins the stacking order. */
/* Anchored to the FOOT of Janitor's bar rather than its top, so the wordmark
   lands inside the bar whatever height their bar happens to be: the row is
   pulled up by its own height and gives that height straight back to the flow. */
/* Their bar cannot hold an <img> (this profile strips every CSS image
   reference, and the markup of that bar is not ours to edit). So the site's
   wordmark and horseshoe are drawn as a fixed layer at the top of the viewport
   with the largest z-index there is: their own bar stays exactly as Janitor
   paints it underneath, buttons and caption included, and the two marks sit on
   it. Height follows a 44-52px bar, which is what the live site uses. */
.uma-hdr {
  position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; z-index: 2147483647;
  height: 57px; margin: 0;
  display: flex; align-items: flex-start; justify-content: space-between;
  padding: 0; background: #0F57FB; pointer-events: none;
}
.uma-hdr-brand { display: block; line-height: 0; }
/* narrow phones: the label must not creep into the first plate, nor the
   accounts row crowd itself */
@media (max-width: 379px) {
  .uma-playnow { padding-right: 5px; }
  .uma-acc .uma-fan-lbl { font-size: 11px; }
  .uma-acc .uma-fan-links { gap: 6px; }
  .uma-acc .uma-fan-links img { max-height: 26px; }
  .uma-acc .uma-fan-links a:first-child img { max-height: 17px; }
}
/* .header__wrapper .-logo: width 32.5333vw, margin-left 4vw */
/* .header__wrapper .-logo.is-top.is-large on the site: the mark starts larger
   than the bar and settles down to its normal width once the page moves. */
/* .header__wrapper .-logo, measured off two screenshots of the official page
   (1260 px wide, 360 CSS px, DPR 3.5):
     settled   box 117.0 x 34.6 css at x 14.9, y 103.5  -> 32.51vw
     at rest   box 199.9 x 59.0 css at x 15.7, y 104.0  -> 55.53vw
   So: left 4vw, top 10px, and only the width changes as the page moves. The
   mark is anchored near the top rather than centred, which is why the larger
   one hangs out of the 57px bar and the small one does not. */
.uma-hdr-brand img {
  display: block; width: 32.5333vw; height: auto;
  margin-left: 4vw; margin-top: 10px;
}
/* A scroll timeline cannot attach to this layer: the band is position:fixed and
   Chrome resolves a fixed subtree against the viewport, so scroll() has nothing
   to follow (verified in a harness built on Janitor's own stylesheet and
   markup). A *view* timeline is a different animal — it tracks the box of an
   element that really is in the flow — so a zero-height sentinel parked one
   screen down -- less the height of Janitor's own bar, which is what the shell
   starts under -- gives us "0 at the top of the page, 1 after V px of scroll". timeline-scope hoists that name up to the shell so the fixed
   wordmark can reference it. */
.uma-shell { timeline-scope: --uma-settle; }
.uma-sentinel {
  position: absolute; left: 0; top: calc(100vh - 64px); width: 0; height: 0;
  view-timeline: --uma-settle block; pointer-events: none;
}
@supports (animation-timeline: --uma-settle) {
  @keyframes uma-logo-settle {
    from { width: 55.5333vw; }
    to   { width: 32.5333vw; }
  }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
    .uma-hdr-brand img {
      animation: uma-logo-settle linear both;
      animation-timeline: --uma-settle;
      animation-range: cover 0% cover 14%;
    }
  }
}

   Janitor (a wrapper inside the item carries a solid fill, which is why the
   `background: transparent` on the item itself never reached it), and the sheet
   ended in nothing. The official menu (umamusume.com, 205210) ends in a cream
   card with badges on it and a row of circular social buttons. So: no grey
   survives anywhere in the sheet, the unread row becomes a lighter blue, and
   the foot borrows the official furniture — the note about how this profile was
   built sits in the cream card where the download badges sit on the site, and
   the site's circular social row sits under it. */

/* no grey in the sheet: whatever Janitor paints behind a row goes transparent */
[class*="otificationsPopover"] [class*="otificationItem"],
[class*="otificationsPopover"] [class*="otificationItem"] *,
[class*="otificationsPopover"] [class*="otificationsList"] > div {
  background-color: transparent !important;
  background-image: none !important;
}
/* an unread row is a lighter blue, not a grey card */
[class*="otificationsPopover"] [class*="nread"],
[class*="otificationsPopover"] [data-unread],
[class*="otificationsPopover"] [class*="otificationItem"][class*="nread"] {
  background-color: rgba(255,255,255,.18) !important;
  border-radius: 2.6vw !important;
  box-shadow: inset .9vw 0 0 #F2739E !important;
}
/* hairline between rows, the way the official menu separates its links */
[class*="otificationsPopover"] [class*="otificationItem"] + [class*="otificationItem"] {
  border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.26) !important;
}

/* ---------- the sheet's foot ----------
   The sheet itself, and the link in it, cannot both come from a pseudo-element:
   a `content` string cannot carry an anchor. So the foot is our own markup,
   sitting in the profile but pinned to the viewport, and it exists only while
   Janitor's sheet does — `body:has(...)` is the gate. The sheet reserves the
   same band at its bottom (padding-bottom below) so no row can end up behind
   it. The row above the card is the profile's own accounts, not the game's:
   Saucepan, Discord and Janitor AI, the three the profile already links.
   The card keeps the ground the official card has: pale horseshoes behind the
   words, the same way umamusume.com sets its download card. */
.uma-sheet-foot { display: none; }
body:has([class*="otificationsPopover"]) .uma-sheet-foot {
  display: block;
  position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; z-index: 10060;
  padding: 7vw 4.2vw 3.4vw;

  font-family: roboto, "Roboto Condensed", Arial, sans-serif;
  line-height: 1.35;
}

/* Sections settle in as they arrive, so the page has some life as you scroll.
   Scroll-driven only, and only when the reader has not asked for less motion. */
@supports (animation-timeline: view()) {
  @keyframes uma-reveal {
    from { opacity: .35; transform: translateY(26px); }
    to   { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
  }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
    .uma-sec > .uma-tag-wrap,
    .uma-sec > .uma-hl,
    .uma-sec > .uma-card,
    .uma-sec > .uma-more,
    .uma-sec > .uma-news-frame,
    .uma-sec > .uma-grid,
    .uma-sec > .uma-media-row,
    .uma-sec > .uma-carousel,
    .uma-sec > .uma-fan-rows,
    .uma-sec > .uma-profile-card,
    .uma-sec > .uma-about-txt,
    .uma-sec > .uma-explore {
      animation: uma-reveal linear both;
      animation-timeline: view();
      animation-range: entry 12% entry 52%;
    }
  }
}

    animation-duration: .001ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
    transition-duration: .001ms !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important;
  }
}
